confidence_notes: I based the meal, coffee and beer anchors on one web search of cost-of-living aggregators: mylifeelsewhere, livingcost.org, nomad.watch, citycost.org and travel spending guides. Those sources put an inexpensive meal at about $4, a cappuccino at about $2.4-2.5, local beer at about $1.2-1.5 and a mid-range meal for two at about $17-27. They vary by about 20-30%. I did not search directly for cocktail or wine prices. I estimated them from how they usually compare with beer in the Philippines. Imported wine is relatively expensive there, so these two anchors are less certain. The accommodation figures are my own estimates from general knowledge of Palawan's tourist market. I did not check any booking sites or listings, so they are the least certain. July is the rainy season, which may lower room rates a little. The FX rate is the RBA 4pm fixing for 18 November 2026, the latest observation found when this was generated. It comes from a search result citing the RBA exchange-rates page.
comparable_city_reasoning: Prices are similar to other secondary Philippine tourist cities such as Dumaguete, Iloilo or Cebu outside the business districts. They are slightly above provincial averages because Puerto Princesa is the gateway to the Underground River and El Nido.
